title: The Ambassadors
author: Henry James
description: Chad Newsome has gone to Paris. He is charmed by Old World fascinations and caught up in the leisurely craft and bohemian direction of European worldliness. An older woman of rank and adventurous but subtle skill, Madame de Vionnet, strokes his ego and does her best to keep Chad in Paris indefinitely. Chad's mother lives in Woollett, Mass., and wants her son to return to run the family business. Mrs. Newsome is an invalid and cannot go to Paris to fetch her son herself, so she employs Lambert Strether and Sarah Pocock to return Chad to Massachusetts. Sarah has been to Paris before and is aware of its attractiveness, so her determination to succeed in this task is fixed and uncompromising. Strether is of later middle age, however, and inspired by the fairytale of a beautiful life in Europe.

title: The art of cross-examination
author: Francis Lewis Wellman
description: "Drawing upon his own experiences and upon the brilliant achievements of such noted lawyers as Herbert C. Smyth, Lloyd Paul Stryker, George Z. Medalie, Elihu Root, and Frederic R. Coudert, among others, Francis L. Wellman explains and exemplifies the principles of questioning. He quotes extensively from many memorable cases, utilizing them to illustrate both the manner and matter of cross-examination. He takes up the handling of the perjured witness and the expert, he underscores the importance of sequence, and he offers many insights into the psychology of the witness. He shows how knowing when to elicit information -- and when not to -- are part of the artistry of the advocate"--P. [4] of cover.

title: 婦人衞生雜誌 1903.03 no. 160
author: 大日本婦人衛生会
description: The Fujin Eisei Zasshi (婦人衞生雜誌 "Women's Hygiene Journal") was a Japanese periodical published by the Greater Japan Women's Hygiene Association (大日本婦人衛生会). It was launched in 1888 as the organization's official organ (initially named 婦人衛生会雑誌 until 1893) and lasted until 1926. It was dedicated to the study of women's health and hygiene and is an important historical source in exploring the relationship between modern medicine and the focus on women's bodies as an object of research and a concern of public health. It was also a central publication in the broader rise of the modern concept of hygiene (衛生) and was aimed primarily at educated women readers. Ogino Ginko (荻野吟子 1851-1913), Japan's first female licensed physician, was a key leader in the association and also one of the founding editors of the journal with Matsuura Satoko (松浦里子 1861-1891).

title: 週刊平民新聞 1903.11.15 No. 1
author: 平民社
description: The weekly Heimin Shinbun (平民新聞 "Commoners' Newspaper") was the organ of the Heiminsha (平民社), an important early Japanese socialist association founded by 幸徳秋水 (Kōtoku Shūsui) and 堺利彦 (Sakai Toshihiko) in 1903. Running for sixty-four numbered issues from 15 November 1903 to 29 January 1905. It maintained a standing English-language column on its front page to communicate with foreign socialists, and its first-anniversary issue, no. 53 (13 November 1904), carried the first partial Japanese translation of Marx and Engels's Communist Manifesto, jointly rendered by Sakai and Kōtoku from Samuel Moore's English edition. Subjected to repeated fines, suppressions, and prosecutions throughout 1904, the paper closed with a defiantly all-red final issue on 29 January 1905, modeled on the last number of Marx's Neue Rheinische Zeitung, and was succeeded by a newly named publication Chokugen (直言) until that too was shut down later in the year.

Für Hilferding war die Entwicklung der Aktiengesellschaften und schließlich der Monopole ein wichtiger Schritt über den Kapitalismus der freien Konkurrenz hinaus hin zu einem monopolistischen Kapitalismus. Durch die Monopolisierung und Konzentration werden kleine Unternehmer und kleine Kapitalanleger verdrängt. Durch die zunehmende Verschmelzung von Wirtschaft und Staat komme es zu einem staatsmonopolistischen Kapitalismus. title: 週刊平民新聞 1904.02.14 No. 14
author: 平民社
description: The weekly Heimin Shinbun (平民新聞 "Commoners' Newspaper") was the organ of the Heiminsha (平民社), an important early Japanese socialist association founded by 幸徳秋水 (Kōtoku Shūsui) and 堺利彦 (Sakai Toshihiko) in 1903. Running for sixty-four numbered issues from 15 November 1903 to 29 January 1905. It maintained a standing English-language column on its front page to communicate with foreign socialists, and its first-anniversary issue, no. 53 (13 November 1904), carried the first partial Japanese translation of Marx and Engels's Communist Manifesto, jointly rendered by Sakai and Kōtoku from Samuel Moore's English edition. Subjected to repeated fines, suppressions, and prosecutions throughout 1904, the paper closed with a defiantly all-red final issue on 29 January 1905, modeled on the last number of Marx's Neue Rheinische Zeitung, and was succeeded by a newly named publication Chokugen (直言) until that too was shut down later in the year.

Stripped of all her belongings but for one set of clothes and a doll, Sara becomes a servant of the household. Hated by the schoolmistress for her independent spirit, Sara becomes a pariah in the household, with only a few secretly loyal friends. But through her inner integrity and strength of will, Sara Crewe maintains the deportment, inner nobility and generous spirit of a "real" princess.

title: ERIC ED619960: Report of the Commissioner of Education for the Year 1903. Volume 1
author: ERIC
description: The Commissioner's introduction to Volume 1 includes state school system statistics. Chapter I addresses vacation schools, playgrounds, and settlements, with discussion of poor children in major cities, playground conditions, playground social conditions, play psychology, and settlement-movement history. Subsequent chapters cover laws concerning agricultural and mechanical land-grant colleges, British and Irish education, London school board education administration, and American universities. Chapter VI offers education articles by early English writers. Denver Superintendent of Schools Aaron Gove gives an overview of U.S. public school systems in Chapter VII. Subsequent chapters cover the Southern educational movement; common school establishment in West Virginia, Maryland, Virginia, and Delaware between 1863 and 1900; current teacher-certification status; secondary education, including its history and current issues; and French education. Consular reports in Chapter XIV concern the Hebrew school of agriculture in Germany, the German colonial school in Witzenhausen, Saxon commercial education progress, continental European commercial education, German industrial and trade schools, school savings banks, technical education's influence, Quebec agriculture schools, education and crime elimination, European industrial education, the Moseley Industrial Commission inquiry, Japan's prison population, public school in the German Empire and in Prussia, German girls' commercial education, Liberia's education system, German industrial supplementary schools, women's admission to a German university, medical supervision of Berlin and Paris schools, and Russian schools. Subsequent chapters cover a list of foreign institutions of higher education; kindergarten; physical training; public, society, and school libraries; U.S. manual, industrial, and technical training; U.S. school and college coeducation; U.S. Catholic schools; state normal schools; the Bureau of Education's exhibit at the Louisiana Purchase Exhibition; a list of education periodicals; and a directory of chief state school officers, city superintendents, presidents of men's and coeducational liberal arts colleges, women's college presidents, technology school presidents, and principals of public and private normal schools. [For Volume 2, see ED619961.]

The sequel to *King Coal* was posthumously published under the title, *The Coal War*. (Source: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/King_Coal))

The book mentions the critical report by the missionary William Henry Sheppard on an 1899 massacre of over eighty people by Zappo Zaps sent to collect taxes. title: The plays of Oscar Wilde
author: Oscar Wilde
description: Oscar Wilde took London by storm with his first comedy, Lady Windermere's Fan. The combination of dazzling wit, subtle social criticism, sumptuous settings and the theme of a guilty secret proved a winner, both here and in his next three plays, A Woman of No Importance, An Ideal Husband, and his undisputed masterpiece, The Importance of Being Earnest. This volume includes all Wilde's plays from his early tragedy Vera to the controversial Salome and the little known fragments, La Sainte Courtisane and A Florentine Tragedy. The edition affords a rare chance to see Wilde's best known work in the context of his entire dramatic output, and to appreciate plays which have hitherto received scant critical attention.

description: The Fujin Eisei Zasshi (婦人衞生雜誌 "Women's Hygiene Journal") was a Japanese periodical published by the Greater Japan Women's Hygiene Association (大日本婦人衛生会). It was launched in 1888 as the organization's official organ (initially named 婦人衛生会雑誌 until 1893) and lasted until 1926. It was dedicated to the study of women's health and hygiene and is an important historical source in exploring the relationship between modern medicine and the focus on women's bodies as an object of research and a concern of public health. It was also a central publication in the broader rise of the modern concept of hygiene (衛生) and was aimed primarily at educated women readers. Ogino Ginko (荻野吟子 1851-1913), Japan's first female licensed physician, was a key leader in the association and also one of the founding editors of the journal with Matsuura Satoko (松浦里子 1861-1891).

title: Imre
author: Edward Prime-Stevenson
description: Early moving novel about the meeting of two gay men who gradually fall in love and wind up happily together: a shocker for 1906. Described by the author as "a little psychological romance", the narrative follows two men who by chance meet at a cafe in Budapest, Hungary. Both Oswald, a 30-something British aristocrat, and Imre, a 25-year-old Hungarian military officer, are "insistently masculine types tempered by a love of art". Over the course of several months they forge a friendship that leads to a series of cautious revelations and disclosures, and ultimately love.

title: In the days of the comet
author: H. G. Wells
description: H. G. Wells, in his 1906 In the Days of the Comet uses the vapors of a comet to trigger a deep and lasting change in humanity's perspective on themselves and the world. In the build-up to a great war, poor student William Leadford struggles against the harsh conditions the lower-class live under. He also falls in love with a middle-class girl named Nettie. But when he discovers that Nettie has eloped with a man of upper-class standing, William struggles with the betrayal, and in the disorder of his own mind decides to buy a revolver and kill them both. All through this a large comet lights the night sky with a green glow, bright enough that the street lamps are left unlit.

title: Looking backward
author: Edward Bellamy
description: Bellamy's novel tells the story of a hero figure named Julian West, a young American, who towards the end of the 19th century, falls into a deep, hypnosis-induced sleep and wakes up 113 years later. He finds himself in the same location (Boston, Massachusetts), but in a totally changed world: It is the year 2000, and while he was sleeping, the United States has been transformed into a socialist utopia. The remainder of the book outlines Bellamy's thoughts about improving the future. The major themes include problems associated with capitalism, a proposed socialist solution of a nationalization of all industry, and the use of an "industrial army" to organize production and distribution, as well as how to ensure free cultural production under such conditions.

From the August-December 1906 issue of "Overland Monthly: an illustrated magazine of the west." Volume XLVIII. Features several photos of O'Neil, her residences, her pets, and her Japanese maid Tolo. Includes photos of O'Neil on the property of her Tyngsboro, Massachusetts residence which she reportedly purchased in 1904, listed for sale in 1907, and successfully sold the property to the Sisters of Notre Dame on October 24, 1908 (Lowell Annals, 1905-1917). There are not many surviving photos from this property, likely because it was never a primary residence and rather a vacation home she retreated to in between touring contracts.

title: The Spirit of the Border
author: Zane Grey
description: Wikipedia: **Spirit of the Border** is an historical novel written by Zane Grey, first published in 1906. The novel is based on events occurring in the Ohio River Valley in the late eighteenth century. It features the exploits of Lewis Wetzel, a historical personage who had dedicated his life to the destruction of Native Americans and to the protection of nascent white settlements in that region. The story deals with the attempt by Moravian Church missionaries to Christianize Indians and how two brothers' lives take different paths upon their arrival on the border. A highly romanticized account, the novel is the second in a trilogy, the first of which is **Betty Zane**, Gray's first published work, and **The Last Trail**, which focuses on the life of Jonathan Zane, Gray's ancestor.

Mead examines the Corpus Hermeticum , the Asclepius , and related writings, showing how Hermeticism influenced early Christian mysticism, Gnosticism, and Renaissance philosophy. He also explores the concept of the "divine man" and the role of secret wisdom in antiquity. This volume is essential reading for students of esoteric traditions, Neoplatonism, and the philosophical undercurrents of Western spirituality.

title: 婦人衞生雜誌 1906.06 no. 199
author: 大日本婦人衛生会
description: The Fujin Eisei Zasshi (婦人衞生雜誌 "Women's Hygiene Journal") was a Japanese periodical published by the Greater Japan Women's Hygiene Association (大日本婦人衛生会). It was launched in 1888 as the organization's official organ (initially named 婦人衛生会雑誌 until 1893) and lasted until 1926. It was dedicated to the study of women's health and hygiene and is an important historical source in exploring the relationship between modern medicine and the focus on women's bodies as an object of research and a concern of public health. It was also a central publication in the broader rise of the modern concept of hygiene (衛生) and was aimed primarily at educated women readers. Ogino Ginko (荻野吟子 1851-1913), Japan's first female licensed physician, was a key leader in the association and also one of the founding editors of the journal with Matsuura Satoko (松浦里子 1861-1891).

author: Henri Bergson, CHAILLAND
description: French philosopher Henri Bergson's Creative Evolution was published in 1907 and translated into English in 1911. Very popular at the time, it gives an alternate mechanism for evolution - that it is motivated by an "elan vital" a vital impetus, also graspable as our natural creative urge. It also looks at Bergson's conception of time, a subjective "duration" (rather than the quantifiable time of a clock) that is best understood not through the intellect but through our creative intuition, an idea that influenced Marcel Proust and other modernist thinkers.

description: As creeping secularism and godless humanism triumph over traditional morality, it creates a world that has been divided into three powerblocks, where religious doctrine is not tolerated and euthanasia is practiced widely. In Britain, the Royal Family has been deposed; institutions of higher learning have been closed, and a politician intent on power in the name of peace is intent on the destruction of religion. The world now has only three main religious forces: Catholicism, Secular Humanism, and "the Eastern religions." As a shrinking Church stands resolutely against him, laws are passed which require all the world's people to formally disavow the existence of God or be executed without trial.

title: Ma double vie
author: Sarah Bernhardt
description: My Double Life is the autobiography of the French actress Sarah Bernhardt, who was internationally famed during her lifetime and afterwards as one of the classical theater's all-time greatest stars. Bernhardt's memoirs are composed with a novelist's (or actress's) sense of artistry and suspense that leaves no doubt of the charisma for which she was famed in her "double life," both on- and offstage. Yet at the same time as this book very consciously contributes to the crafting of her image, it also illuminates a whole era: not only the world of theater, but also the worlds of women, politics, society, Europe and America, and, indeed, of history making itself.

description: "The Pit and the Pendulum" is a short story by American writer Edgar Allan Poe and first published in 1842 in the literary annual The Gift: A Christmas and New Year's Present for 1843. The story is about the torments endured by a prisoner of the Spanish Inquisition, though Poe skews historical facts. The narrator of the story describes his experience of being tortured. The story is especially effective at inspiring fear in the reader because of its heavy focus on the senses, such as sound, emphasizing its reality, unlike many of Poe's stories which are aided by the supernatural. The traditional elements established in popular horror tales at the time are followed, but critical reception has been mixed. The tale has been adapted to film several times.

The story is set in London in 1886 and deals with Mr. Adolf Verloc and his work as a spy for an unnamed country (presumably Russia). The Secret Agent is one of Conrad's later political novels in which he moved away from his former tales of seafaring. The novel is dedicated to H. G. Wells and deals broadly with anarchism, espionage, and terrorism. It also deals with exploitation of the vulnerable in Verloc's relationship with his brother-in-law Stevie, who has an intellectual disability. Conrad’s gloomy portrait of London depicted in the novel was influenced by Charles Dickens’ *Bleak House*. (Source: [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Secret_Agent))

description: The Fujin Eisei Zasshi (婦人衞生雜誌 "Women's Hygiene Journal") was a Japanese periodical published by the Greater Japan Women's Hygiene Association (大日本婦人衛生会). It was launched in 1888 as the organization's official organ (initially named 婦人衛生会雑誌 until 1893) and lasted until 1926. It was dedicated to the study of women's health and hygiene and is an important historical source in exploring the relationship between modern medicine and the focus on women's bodies as an object of research and a concern of public health. It was also a central publication in the broader rise of the modern concept of hygiene (衛生) and was aimed primarily at educated women readers. Ogino Ginko (荻野吟子 1851-1913), Japan's first female licensed physician, was a key leader in the association and also one of the founding editors of the journal with Matsuura Satoko (松浦里子 1861-1891).

Troeltsch, Ernst: „Über historische und dogmatische Methode in der Theologie“ [1908]. In: ders.: Zur religiösen Lage, Religionsphilosophie und Ethik. Gesammelte Schriften, Bd. II, Tübingen, Mohr, 1913, S. 729-753. Ernst Troeltsch explicates the methodological foundations of history as a science. Leopold von Ranke could still believe history could play in the greatest possible objectivity, "as it's been really" is. This is no possibility in the result of historicism debate, the debate over historicism and its criticism. In the methodological reflection the fakta no longer can be seen in that innocence. This will be rescheduled for the study of history, what was preceded by philosophy: the objectivity of the objects is problematic, their respective assessment is debatable, and therefore in need of explicit criteria. Ernst Troeltsch puts together a triad of basic principles of historical-critical research: Methodological doubt, analogy and correlation. Ernst Troeltsch expliziert die methodologischen Grundlagen von Geschichte als Wissenschaft. Durfte Leopold von Ranke noch glauben, Geschichtsschreibung könne in möglichst großer Objektivität wiedergeben, "wie es eigentlich gewesen" sei, setzt im Ergebnis der Historismus-Debatte, der Debatte um den Historismus und dessen Kritik, die methodologische Reflexion ein, da die Fakta nicht mehr in jener Unschuld gesehen werden können. Damit wird für die Geschichtswissenschaft nachgeholt, worin Philosophie voraus ging: Die Objektivität der Objekte wird problematisch, deren jeweilige Bewertung wird diskutabel und mithin expliziter Kriterien bedürftig. Ernst Troeltsch stellt eine Trias von Grundprinzipien historisch-kritischer Forschung zusammen: Methodischer Zweifel, Analogie und Korrelation.

description: Think that the problem of large corporations exercising undue influence in the political sphere is a recent phenomenon? If so, think again. Mr. Crewe's Career, an eye-opening historical novel set in the early twentieth century, follows the efforts of the railroad industry to steamroll its way into state politics in New Hampshire. This partly autobiographical political novel, set in New Hampshire, is a warning against the powers of the railroad interests to control elected government. Churchill himself had run for governor just two years earlier and had met his defeat at the hands of the state's railroad lobby. title: My African Journey
author: Winston S. Churchill
description: "As Undersecretary of State for the Colonies, Winston Churchill toured Britain's territories in East Africa. This book documents his travels and the people he met; he waxes lyrical on the natural beauty of Uganda and goes on to explore Egypt and Sudan via the White Nile. More that a travelogue however, Churchill, now in his 30s, turns his attention towards issues of government and development, suggesting that the best way to tap the latent wealth of East Africa was the development of the railway system. His ruminations on settlement, race and government provide an intriguing insight into contemporary imperialism of interest to scholars and students of African history and British colonialism."--Bloomsbury Publishing.

The expression of the soul by means of the brain and body is what we call the art of 'living.' We certainly do not learn this art at school to any appreciable extent. title: The Kybalion A Study Of The Hermetic Philosophy Of Ancient Egypt And Greece
author: Three Initiates
description: The Kybalion – A Study of the Hermetic Philosophy of Ancient Egypt and Greece అనేది Hermetic Philosophy (హెర్మెటిక్ తత్వశాస్త్రం) గురించి ప్రసిద్ధి చెందిన ఒక ఆధునిక ఆధ్యాత్మిక గ్రంథం. ఇది “Three Initiates” అనే కలం పేరుతో 1908లో ప్రచురించబడింది. 📖 ఈ పుస్తకం దేనికి సంబంధించినది? The Kybalion ప్రధానంగా Hermeticism అనే తాత్విక–ఆధ్యాత్మిక సంప్రదాయంలోని కొన్ని భావాలను వివరిస్తుంది. పుస్తకం తన బోధనలను ప్రాచీన ఈజిప్టు మరియు గ్రీస్‌కు చెందిన Hermes Trismegistus సంప్రదాయంతో అనుసంధానిస్తుంది. అయితే ఒక ముఖ్యమైన విషయం: ఇది ప్రాచీన ఈజిప్టు గ్రంథం కాదు. 1908లో ప్రచురించబడిన ఆధునిక పుస్తకం. ఇందులోని “Seven Hermetic Principles” ను ప్రాచీన హెర్మెటిక్ గ్రంథాల నుంచి నేరుగా తీసుకున్నవిగా భావించడం చారిత్రకంగా సరైనది కాదు. ============================ ది 1908లో “Three Initiates” అనే కలం పేరుతో వచ్చిన ఆధునిక గ్రంథం; కాబట్టి ఇందులోని భావాలను ప్రాచీన వేద/ఉపనిషత్ సిద్ధాంతాలతో సారూప్యతగా మాత్రమే పోల్చాలి, “ఇవి రెండూ ఒకటే” అని కాదు. క్రింద మొత్తం పుస్తకానికి Chapter-wise Telugu Guide ఇస్తున్నాను. 📖 The Kybalion — అధ్యాయం వారీగా తెలుగు వివరణ Chapter 1 — THE HERMETIC PHILOSOPHY హెర్మెటిక్ తత్వశాస్త్రం పరిచయం మూల భావం: ప్రపంచం, ప్రకృతి, మనిషి, చైతన్యం గురించి ఒక అంతర్గత తాత్విక జ్ఞానం ఉందని గ్రంథం పరిచయం చేస్తుంది. దీనిని Hermes Trismegistus సంప్రదాయంతో అనుసంధానిస్తుంది. సులభమైన ఉదాహరణ: మన కళ్లకు కనిపించేది ఒక సంఘటన; దాని వెనుక ఉన్న కారణాన్ని తెలుసుకోవడం తాత్విక పరిశీలన. భారతీయ పోలిక: ఉపనిషత్తులు కూడా “నేను ఎవరు? జగత్తు స్వభావం ఏమిటి?” వంటి ప్రశ్నలను పరిశీలిస్తాయి. ఆచరణ: ఏ విషయాన్నైనా పైకి కనిపించినంత మాత్రాన నమ్మకుండా, “దీని వెనుక కారణం ఏమిటి?” అని ప్రశ్నించడం. Chapter 2 — THE SEVEN HERMETIC PRINCIPLES ఏడు హెర్మెటిక్ సూత్రాలు ఇది పుస్తకంలోని అత్యంత ముఖ్యమైన అధ్యాయం. ఏడు సూత్రాలు: Mentalism — మానసికత Correspondence — సారూప్యత Vibration — కంపనం Polarity — ధ్రువత్వం Rhythm — లయ Cause & Effect — కారణ–ఫలితం Gender — సృజనాత్మక ద్వంద్వత్వం భారతీయ పోలిక: కర్మ, ద్వంద్వం, ప్రకృతి చక్రాలు, చైతన్యం వంటి భావాలతో కొన్ని పోలికలు కనిపిస్తాయి. ఆచరణ: ఈ ఏడు సూత్రాలను జీవితాన్ని పరిశీలించే **ఏడు “లెన్స్‌లు”**గా ఉపయోగించుకోవచ్చు. Chapter 3 — MENTALISM “The All is Mind” మూల భావం: విశ్వాన్ని అర్థం చేసుకోవడంలో Mind/Consciousness కు ప్రాధాన్యత ఉందని Kybalion చెబుతుంది. ఉదాహరణ: ఒకే సంఘటన ఇద్దరికి జరిగినా, వారి ఆలోచనా విధానం వేరు కావడం వల్ల అనుభవం వేరుగా ఉంటుంది. భారతీయ పోలిక: “మనస్సు” గురించి ఉపనిషత్తులు, యోగశాస్త్రం, వేదాంతం విస్తృతంగా చర్చిస్తాయి. అయితే Kybalion Mentalism = అద్వైత వేదాంత బ్రహ్మం అని నేరుగా చెప్పడం సరైంది కాదు. ఆచరణ: రోజుకు 10 నిమిషాలు మీ ఆలోచనలను గమనించండి. ప్రశ్న: “నేను నా ఆలోచనలను గమనిస్తున్నానా? లేక ఆలోచనలే నన్ను నడిపిస్తున్నాయా?” Chapter 4 — THE ALL “The All” అంటే ఏమిటి? మూల భావం: Hermetic తత్వంలో సమస్త అస్తిత్వానికి మూలమైన పరమ వాస్తవాన్ని The All అని పిలుస్తుంది. దాన్ని పరిమిత మానవ రూపంలో ఊహించడం కష్టమని గ్రంథం చెబుతుంది. భారతీయ పోలిక: ఇక్కడ బ్రహ్మం అనే వేదాంత భావనతో కొంత పోలిక కనిపిస్తుంది. కానీ: The All ≠ Brahman అని చారిత్రకంగా సమీకరించకూడదు. ఆచరణ: “నేను–ప్రపంచం” అనే విభజనను కొంతకాలం పక్కన పెట్టి సమస్త జీవుల పరస్పర సంబంధాన్ని పరిశీలించండి. Chapter 5 — THE MENTAL UNIVERSE మూల భావం: విశ్వాన్ని ఒక రకమైన mental creation / mental universe దృష్టితో చూడటమే ఈ అధ్యాయం. మనిషి తన ఆలోచనా ప్రపంచాన్ని ఎలా నిర్మించుకుంటాడో కూడా ఇది వివరిస్తుంది. ఉదాహరణ: “నేను ఎప్పుడూ విఫలమవుతాను” అనే నమ్మకం → భయం → ప్రయత్నం తగ్గడం → ఫలితం చెడిపోవడం. భారతీయ పోలిక: యోగశాస్త్రంలో చిత్తవృత్తులు , మనస్సు ప్రభావం వంటి భావనలు ఉన్నాయి. ఆచరణ: ప్రతికూల ఆలోచన వచ్చినప్పుడు: ఆలోచన → పరిశీలన → నిజమా? → ప్రత్యామ్నాయ దృక్కోణం అని పరిశీలించండి. Chapter 6 — THE DIVINE PARADOX మూల భావం: వాస్తవాన్ని వివరించేటప్పుడు మనిషికి కొన్ని విరుద్ధంగా కనిపించే విషయాలు ఎదురవుతాయి. ఒక స్థాయిలో ప్రపంచం నిజంగా కనిపిస్తుంది; మరో తాత్విక స్థాయిలో దాని స్వరూపాన్ని వేరుగా పరిశీలించవచ్చు. భారతీయ పోలిక: అద్వైతంలో వ్యవహారిక సత్యం – పరమార్థిక సత్యం వంటి చర్చలు గుర్తుకు రావచ్చు. ఆచరణ: “నా దృక్కోణమే పూర్తిగా నిజం” అనే మొండితనాన్ని తగ్గించుకోవడం. Chapter 7 — “THE ALL” IN ALL మూల భావం: సమస్త అస్తిత్వంలో The All యొక్క ఉనికిని Hermetic దృష్టితో పరిశీలిస్తుంది. ఉదాహరణ: సముద్రంలోని ప్రతి అల సముద్రానికి చెందినదే; అల ప్రత్యేకంగా కనిపించినా సముద్రం నుండి వేరుకాదు. భారతీయ పోలిక: “సర్వం ఖల్విదం బ్రహ్మ” అనే ఉపనిషత్తు భావనతో కొంత సారూప్యతగా చూడవచ్చు. ఆచరణ: ఇతర జీవులను పూర్తిగా వేరైన వస్తువులుగా కాకుండా పరస్పర సంబంధంలో చూడటం. Chapter 8 — PLANES OF CORRESPONDENCE మూల భావం: అస్తిత్వానికి వివిధ స్థాయిలు లేదా planes ఉన్నాయని Hermetic philosophy వివరిస్తుంది. సాధారణంగా: Physical — భౌతిక Mental — మానసిక Spiritual — ఆధ్యాత్మిక అనే విభజనతో ఆలోచించవచ్చు. భారతీయ పోలిక: స్థూల, సూక్ష్మ, కారణ శరీరాల భావనతో కొన్ని పోలికలు కనిపించవచ్చు. ఆచరణ: ఒక సమస్యను కేవలం భౌతికంగా కాకుండా: శరీరం + మనస్సు + విలువలు మూడు కోణాల్లో పరిశీలించండి. Chapter 9 — MENTAL PLANE మూల భావం: ఆలోచనలు, భావనలు, మానసిక స్థితులు ఒక ప్రత్యేక స్థాయిగా పరిశీలించబడతాయి. ఉదాహరణ: ఒక మాట → ఒక ఆలోచన → ఒక భావోద్వేగం → ఒక చర్య. ఆచరణ: మీ కోపాన్ని “నేనే కోపం” అని కాకుండా: “నా మనస్సులో కోపం అనే స్థితి వచ్చింది.” అని గమనించడం. ఇది self-awareness పెంచుతుంది. Chapter 10 — POLARITY మూల భావం: విరుద్ధాలు ఒకదానికొకటి పూర్తిగా వేరైనవి కాకుండా ఒకే continuumలోని రెండు ధ్రువాలుగా ఉండవచ్చని చెబుతుంది. ఉదాహరణ: చలి ←────────→ వేడి అజ్ఞానం ←────────→ జ్ఞానం భారతీయ పోలిక: ద్వంద్వ భావనలతో కొంత పోలిక. ఆచరణ: “నాకు అతనంటే ద్వేషం” అనిపించినప్పుడు: “ఈ భావం ఎంత తీవ్రంగా ఉంది? దీని వ్యతిరేక స్థితి ఏమిటి?” అని పరిశీలించండి. Chapter 11 — RHYTHM మూల భావం: ప్రపంచంలో ఎత్తుపల్లాలు, ముందుకు–వెనుకకు కదలికలు, చక్రాలు ఉంటాయని చెబుతుంది. ఉదాహరణ: సంతోషం → దుఃఖం → సంతోషం లాభం → నష్టం → లాభం భారతీయ పోలిక: కాలచక్రం, ప్రకృతి చక్రాలు వంటి భావనలు గుర్తుకు వస్తాయి. ఆచరణ: కష్టకాలంలో: “ఇది శాశ్వతం కాదు.” అనే అవగాహనను పెంచుకోవడం. Chapter 12 — CAUSATION మూల భావం: ప్రతి ఫలితానికి ఒక కారణం ఉంటుంది. Cause → Effect మనిషి కేవలం పరిస్థితులకు బానిస కాకుండా, కారణాల స్థాయిలో పనిచేయాలని పుస్తకం చెబుతుంది. భారతీయ పోలిక: కర్మ సిద్ధాంతం తో పోలిక కనిపిస్తుంది. కానీ రెండింటినీ పూర్తిగా ఒకటిగా చూడకూడదు. ఆచరణ: “ఎందుకు నాకు ఇలా జరిగింది?” అనే ప్రశ్నకు బదులు: “ఇక నుంచి నేను ఏ కారణాన్ని సృష్టించాలి?” అని ఆలోచించడం. Chapter 13 — GENDER మూల భావం: ఇక్కడ Gender అంటే కేవలం పురుషుడు/స్త్రీ అనే biological classification కాదు. సృష్టిలో active + receptive / masculine + feminine principles ఉన్నాయని Hermetic భావన. భారతీయ పోలిక: పురుష–ప్రకృతి , శివ–శక్తి వంటి తాత్విక భావనలతో కొన్ని పోలికలు కనిపిస్తాయి. ఆచరణ: చర్య మాత్రమే కాదు, స్వీకరణ/పరిశీలన కూడా సృజనాత్మక ప్రక్రియలో భాగమని అర్థం చేసుకోవడం. Chapter 14 — MENTAL GENDER ఇది Chapter 13 భావనను మనస్సు స్థాయికి తీసుకువెళుతుంది. మనిషిలో: ఆలోచన + స్వీకరణ + సృజన అనే ప్రక్రియలు పనిచేస్తాయని వివరిస్తుంది. ఉదాహరణ: ఒక ఆలోచన ↓ దాన్ని మనస్సు స్వీకరించడం ↓ దానిపై పని చేయడం ↓ కొత్త ఫలితం ఆచరణ: ఆలోచన వచ్చిన వెంటనే చర్య చేయకుండా, దాన్ని పరిశీలించి అభివృద్ధి చేయడం. Chapter 15 — HERMETIC AXIOMS ఇది పుస్తకంలోని ఆచరణాత్మక భాగాలలో ఒకటి. ముందు చెప్పిన సూత్రాలను కేవలం తెలుసుకోవడం కాకుండా జీవితంలో ఉపయోగించడం గురించి చెబుతుంది. ముఖ్యమైన ఆలోచన Knowledge + Practice = Transformation తెలుసుకోవడం మాత్రమే సరిపోదు. తెలుసుకోవాలి → అర్థం చేసుకోవాలి → ఆచరించాలి → అనుభవించాలి 🔱 ఏడు సూత్రాలను జీవితంలో ఎలా ఉపయోగించాలి? సూత్రం జీవితంలో ఉపయోగం Mentalism ఆలోచనలను గమనించడం Correspondence పెద్ద–చిన్న వ్యవస్థల సంబంధాన్ని చూడటం Vibration మన అంతర్గత స్థితిని మెరుగుపరచడం Polarity భావోద్వేగాల తీవ్రతను మార్చుకోవడం Rhythm జీవితంలోని ఎత్తుపల్లాలను అంగీకరించడం Cause & Effect కారణాలపై పని చేయడం Gender సృజనాత్మక ప్రక్రియను అర్థం చేసుకోవడం 🕉️ వేదాంతంతో ముఖ్యమైన తేడా The Kybalion చదివేటప్పుడు ఈ తేడాను గుర్తుంచుకోవడం చాలా ముఖ్యం. వేదాలు/ఉపనిషత్తులు → ప్రాచీన భారతీయ శ్రుతి సంప్రదాయం Hermetic texts → ప్రాచీన గ్రీకు–ఈజిప్షియన్ తాత్విక సంప్రదాయం The Kybalion → 1908లో వచ్చిన ఆధునిక Hermetic/occult రచన అందువల్ల The Kybalion లోని ప్రతి భావానికి “ఇదే భగవద్గీతలో ఉంది” అని చెప్పడం కంటే, “ఇక్కడ ఇలాంటి తాత్విక సారూప్యత కనిపిస్తుంది” అని చెప్పడం మరింత సరైన పద్ధతి.

title: The Man Who Was Thursday
author: Gilbert Keith Chesterton
description: Can you trust yourself when you don't know who you are? In a park in London, secret policeman Gabriel Syme strikes up a conversation with an anarchist. Sworn to do his duty, Syme uses his new acquaintance to go undercover in Europe's Central Anarchist Council and infiltrate their deadly mission, even managing to have himself voted to the position of 'Thursday'. When Syme discovers another undercover policeman on the Council, however, he starts to question his role in their operations. And as a desperate chase across Europe begins, his confusion grows, as well as his confidence in his ability to outwit his enemies. But he has still to face the greatest terror that the Council has: a man named Sunday, whose true nature is worse than Syme could ever have imagined...

title: The war in the air
author: H. G. Wells
description: Following the development of massive airships, naive Londoner Bert Smallways becomes accidentally involved in a German plot to invade America by air and reduce New York to rubble. But although bombers devastate the city, they cannot overwhelm the coutnry, and their attack leads not to victory but to the beginning of a new and horrific age for humanity. And so dawns the era of Total War, in which brutal aerial bombardments reduce the great cultures of the twentieth century to nothing. As civilization collapses around Smallways, now stranded in a ruined America, he clings to only one home - that he might return to London and marry the woman he loves.

The daughter of a prominent judge who disapproved of secession, Eliza kept a diary that fully registers the anger and despair of Confederate citizens during the last months of the Civil War. title: 婦人衞生雜誌 1908.04 no. 221
author: 大日本婦人衛生会
description: The Fujin Eisei Zasshi (婦人衞生雜誌 "Women's Hygiene Journal") was a Japanese periodical published by the Greater Japan Women's Hygiene Association (大日本婦人衛生会). It was launched in 1888 as the organization's official organ (initially named 婦人衛生会雑誌 until 1893) and lasted until 1926. It was dedicated to the study of women's health and hygiene and is an important historical source in exploring the relationship between modern medicine and the focus on women's bodies as an object of research and a concern of public health. It was also a central publication in the broader rise of the modern concept of hygiene (衛生) and was aimed primarily at educated women readers. Ogino Ginko (荻野吟子 1851-1913), Japan's first female licensed physician, was a key leader in the association and also one of the founding editors of the journal with Matsuura Satoko (松浦里子 1861-1891).

title: A J Raffles, Gentleman Thief
author: Hornung E W
description: Hornung E W : A J Raffles, Gentleman Thief (collected works) The complete collection of the Raffles stories, comprising twenty-six short stories and a novel. This entertaining collection of crime tales presents the adventures of the elegant A. J. Raffles, man-about-town, thief, and the finest slow bowler of his generation. He indulges his passion for cricket and crime, with the aid of his faithful sidekick, 'Bunny' Manders. From the book jacket -- A J Raffles is undoubtedly a gentleman. He lives in Albany in Piccadilly, and as one of England’s finest cricketers is courted during the day by the great, the rich and the fashionable, and invited to their houses. By night he robs them. His adventures are retailed by Bunny Danvers, his admiring accomplice. These classic tales of ingenuity and subtle revenge provide a vivid and thrilling account of high-class villainy from when Victoria was Queen and Britain had an Empire. Written by Ernest William Hornung (7 June 1866 – 22 March 1921), brother-in-law of Sir Arthur Conan Doyle. Although much of Hornung’s work has fallen into obscurity, his Raffles stories continue to be popular, and have enjoyed many film and television adaptations. Critics have interpreted Raffles as a prototype of the anti-hero in modern crime fiction, and he's seen as a literary forerunner of The Saint, James Bond, and other such characters. Copyright Expired Publication The Raffles stories were first published between 1899 and 1909. This book is in the public domain worldwide, because its author died more than 100 years ago and its complete contents were published prior to 1927. title: 婦人衞生雜誌 1909.04 no. 233
author: 大日本婦人衛生会
description: The Fujin Eisei Zasshi (婦人衞生雜誌 "Women's Hygiene Journal") was a Japanese periodical published by the Greater Japan Women's Hygiene Association (大日本婦人衛生会). It was launched in 1888 as the organization's official organ (initially named 婦人衛生会雑誌 until 1893) and lasted until 1926. It was dedicated to the study of women's health and hygiene and is an important historical source in exploring the relationship between modern medicine and the focus on women's bodies as an object of research and a concern of public health. It was also a central publication in the broader rise of the modern concept of hygiene (衛生) and was aimed primarily at educated women readers. Ogino Ginko (荻野吟子 1851-1913), Japan's first female licensed physician, was a key leader in the association and also one of the founding editors of the journal with Matsuura Satoko (松浦里子 1861-1891).

Through Puck the children are witnesses to tales of English history, subtly called forth by Kipling's brilliant and fluid adventure writing. Kipling's historical imagination extends to a wide variety of stories, many of which blend the ghostly and the familiar, and often anticipate his later writing in their themes: a sense of loss and breakdown, but also healing. author: 大日本婦人衛生会
description: The Fujin Eisei Zasshi (婦人衞生雜誌 "Women's Hygiene Journal") was a Japanese periodical published by the Greater Japan Women's Hygiene Association (大日本婦人衛生会). It was launched in 1888 as the organization's official organ (initially named 婦人衛生会雑誌 until 1893) and lasted until 1926. It was dedicated to the study of women's health and hygiene and is an important historical source in exploring the relationship between modern medicine and the focus on women's bodies as an object of research and a concern of public health. It was also a central publication in the broader rise of the modern concept of hygiene (衛生) and was aimed primarily at educated women readers. Ogino Ginko (荻野吟子 1851-1913), Japan's first female licensed physician, was a key leader in the association and also one of the founding editors of the journal with Matsuura Satoko (松浦里子 1861-1891).

It was launched in 1888 as the organization's official organ (initially named 婦人衛生会雑誌 until 1893) and lasted until 1926. It was dedicated to the study of women's health and hygiene and is an important historical source in exploring the relationship between modern medicine and the focus on women's bodies as an object of research and a concern of public health. It was also a central publication in the broader rise of the modern concept of hygiene (衛生) and was aimed primarily at educated women readers. Ogino Ginko (荻野吟子 1851-1913), Japan's first female licensed physician, was a key leader in the association and also one of the founding editors of the journal with Matsuura Satoko (松浦里子 1861-1891).

title: ERIC ED542931: Opportunities for Graduate Study in Agriculture in the United States. Bulletin, 1911, No. 2. Whole Number 447
author: ERIC
description: This bulletin, describing the opportunities in the United States for graduate study in agriculture and those closely allied sciences which have a direct application in agriculture, is the result of an inquiry made by the Bureau of Education in cooperation with the committee on graduate study of the Association of American Agricultural Colleges and Experiment Stations. The inquiry was confined to the agricultural and mechanical colleges, the State universities, and the institutions represented in the Association of American Universities. The bulletin lists courses offered for graduate students only and also those courses open to advanced undergraduates which may be taken by graduate students as major subjects for advanced degrees. No course is listed from any institution whose entrance requirements for 1911 are less than 14 units of high-school work--that is, the equivalent of the standard four-year high-school course--with the exception of the agricultural colleges of the University of Tennessee and Ohio State University, both of which require 12 units for admission. The subject matter of this bulletin is grouped under 19 headings, under which are included the names of the institutions offering courses on some phase of the subjects indicated in the headings. Following the names of the institutions are statements intended to indicate the scope of the work offered by the institution rather than the exact titles of the individual courses. As a supplementary statement to the courses listed, it may be said that opportunity for original study, investigation, and research on special topics is given under certain restrictions by most of these colleges. Under the headings botany, zoology, and the other general sciences, only such courses are listed as seem to have a direct bearing upon agriculture and may therefore be regarded as agricultural-science courses. Many courses are given under two separate headings where such cross reference seems likely to be helpful. [Best copy available has been provided.]

title: ERIC ED542939: Bibliography of Education for 1909-10. Bulletin, 1911, No. 10. Whole Number 456
author: ERIC
description: The bibliography of education for 1909-10, as was its immediate predecessor in the series, has been compiled in the library division of the Bureau of Education, which has been aided, in completing the principal sections of the list, by criticisms and additions furnished by prominent educational specialists. In addition to these collaborators in special classes, the entire bibliography, in its preliminary form, was submitted for revision and additions to the librarians of two of the leading pedagogical collections in the country outside of Washington. A period marked by extensive and excellent literary productivity in education, namely, that reaching from July 1, 1909, to June 30, 1910, falls within the scope of this bibliography; but for special reasons a few important titles published earlier or later than these dates have been included. The aim has been to present a thoroughly representative selection from the main classes of educational literature published in English during this period. Of publications in foreign languages, those which were judged to have special significance for American educators have been mentioned. It is believed that the list here given of current proceedings and reports of educational associations will be found especially comprehensive. References have also been made to a considerable number of State and city school documents of importance appealing during the year. Wherever found desirable and practicable, descriptive and critical annotations, either original or quoted from authoritative reviews, have been appended to the titles of books or articles. An author and subject index is included. [Best copy available has been provided.]

Omkring 1806 møder Bendte kronprinsregenten, den senere Frederik VI (1768-1839), som (muligvis tilskyndet af en af sine nære embedsmænd) tager hende som maitresse – et forhold, der med kortere og længere mellemrum varer resten af Frederik VI.s liv, og gør Bendte Mortensdatter til Frederikke Benedicte Dannemand. I denne, den suverænt længste og grundigste af de fire romaner i serien I tronens skygge giver Ewald på grundlag af myter, rygter, fakta og egen historisk forskning (han var noget af en specialist i netop denne periode af Danmarkshistorien) en fremstilling af det til tider stormfulde forhold mellem de to – Danmarks sidste enevoldskonge og den kvinde, der var den sidste officielle kongelige maitresse – i en periode, der så Napoleonskrigene, Wienerkongressen, statsbankerotten, tabet af Norge og begyndelsen til en fri forfatning og det konstitutionelle monarki, vi kender i dag.

author: Herbert Croly
description: "The Promise of American Life was first published in 1909. It had an immediate and extensive influence on what social historians call the Progressive Era. At the dawn of the New Deal Era, Felix Frankfurter wrote that Croly's book became "a reservoir for all political writings after its publication. Roosevelt's New Nationalism was countered by Wilson's New Freedom, but both derived from Croly."While this may have been hyperbole, it is also a reflection of the impact The Promise made on intellectuals coming of age in the days of doubt and hope just before the Fust World War. author: W. E. B. Du Bois, H. S. De Lay
description: "Shaped by the author's belief that capitalism inexorably led to the exploitation of Southern farmers during Reconstruction, 'The Quest of the Silver Fleece' dramatizes the economic conflict between cotton growers and Northern capitalists. W.E.B. Du Bois uses Miss Sarah Smith's controversial school for Southern black children as the fictional device that links wealthy cotton planters, their exploited black laborers, and the interests of Wall Street and Washington"--Page 4 of cover.

title: The religion of the ancient Celts
author: John Arnott MacCulloch
description: To summon a dead religion from its forgotten grave and to make it tell its story, would require an enchanter's wand. Other old faiths, of Egypt, Babylon, Greece, Rome, are known to us. But in their case liturgies, myths, theogonies, theologies, and the accessories of cult, remain to yield their report of the outward form of human belief and aspiration. How scanty, on the other hand, are the records of Celtic religion! title: The Sea Fairies
author: L. Frank Baum
description: This is a tale of life beneath the sea, of mermaids and sea serpents and other strange inhabitants of the ocean depths. A little girl named Trot and Cap'n Bill, an old sailor, are invited by several mermaids to come and visit their under-water home. Baum wrote this story in the hope of interesting his readers in something other than Oz; in the preface he writes: "I hope my readers who have so long followed Dorothy's adventures in the Land of Oz will be interested in Trot's equally strange experiences." Of course, he did not succeed in distracting his fans from Oz, yet the book was eagerly read; the result of this attempt was that he was forced to introduce Trot and Cap'n Bill into the later Oz stories.

description: This novel is the first in the Wolves Chronicles (aka The Wolves of Willoughby Chase Series), a series of children's novels set during the fictional early-19th century reign of King James the third. A large number of wolves have migrated from the bitter cold of Europe and Russia into Britain via a new "channel tunnel", and terrorize the inhabitants of rural areas. Read about the adventures of cousins Bonnie and Sylvia and their friend Simon the goose-boy as they thwart the evil schemes of their governess Miss Slighcarp, and their so called "teacher" at boarding school, Mrs. Brisket. The story was made into a film in 1989.

These spirited tales convey in a realistic way, the wonderful advances in land and sea locomotion and other successful inventions. Stories like these are impressed upon the memory and their reading is productive only of good. title: U.S. Statutes at Large, Volume 37 (1911-1913), 62nd Congress.
author: U.S. Congress
description: The United States Statutes at Large is the collection of every law, public and private, ever enacted by the Congress, published in order of the date of its passage. These laws are codified every six years in the United States Code, but the Statutes at Large remains the official source of legislation. Until 1948, all treaties and international agreements approved by the Senate were also published in the set. In addition, the Statutes at Large includes the text of the Declaration of Independence, Articles of Confederation, the Constitution, amendments to the Constitution, treaties with Indians and foreign nations, and presidential proclamations.

title: Washington Chapel Chronicle 4, no. 2 (May 1911): 9-16
author: W. Herbert Burk Washington Chapel Guild Emma W. Crawford
description: The May 15, 1911, issue of the Washington Chapel Chronicle (Vol. IV, No. 2), published by the Washington Chapel Guild at the Washington Memorial Chapel in Valley Forge, Pennsylvania, commemorates the 50th anniversary of President Lincoln’s first call for Union defenders, highlighting progress on the Defenders’ Gate, the chapel’s formal admission to the Diocese of Pennsylvania, and contributions to its museum and cemetery. Below is a summary of the key content: 1. Fiftieth Anniversary of Lincoln’s Call and Defenders’ Gate Context : Theodore Roosevelt’s 1904 Valley Forge address, comparing Gettysburg and Valley Forge as critical to national survival, inspired the Defenders’ Gate. The cornerstone was laid on Memorial Day 1910, with hopes of completion within a year. Progress : On April 15, 1911, the 50th anniversary of Lincoln’s call, the first stone of the Lincoln Arch was laid, officiated by Rev. W. Herbert Burk. Masonry work on the lodge began April 26, with foundations completed to the sill line, though work was suspended pending frame preparation. Contracts were confirmed with Evans & Boyer (masonry, $1,722) and William M. Sullivan (cut stone, $2,446), with an estimated total cost of $8,000. Support : The Grand Army of the Republic endorsed the project, with contributions from 43 posts across Pennsylvania, New Jersey, New York, Ohio, Delaware, Illinois, and Michigan, including Stevens Post No. 69, George G. Meade Post No. 1, and William McKinley Post No. 203. Individual donors included Mary M. Hibbs, Gen. Louis Wagner, and Burk. Significance : The gate symbolizes national unity, with calls for patriotic support to complete this monument. 2. Diocesan Recognition and Church Club Visit Convention : At the 127th Convention of the Diocese of Pennsylvania (May 9–10, 1911, Church of St. Luke and the Epiphany, Philadelphia), Burk presented the chapel’s charter, which was approved by the Committee on Charters, formally admitting the Washington Memorial Parish to the convention. Delegates Thomas H. Dobson, Charles Wells Walker, and Nathan B. Hughes were recognized, though Hughes was absent. Church Clubs : On May 2–3, the Church Clubs of Philadelphia visited Valley Forge by automobile, led by Burk, who spoke briefly in the chapel. Major Deakyne, overseeing a national arch, presented its design. The Guild served refreshments, and Burk prioritized the visit over a Sunday school engagement. 3. Washington’s Marquee and Valley Forge Plate Marquee : Last winter, Burk had Washington’s Marquee moved from the Valley Forge Museum to be photographed in snow, replicating its 1777 setup with original poles and pins. Photos by Russa and Burk were copyrighted and used by the Taylor Art Company for a colored postal card featuring the Commander-in-Chief’s standard. Plate : Gus Egolf of Norristown produced a Valley Forge plate with blue-on-white views of Washington’s Headquarters, Wayne Monument, Washington at Prayer, Waterman Monument, Old Penn School, the chapel, and a soldiers’ hut, inscribed with Cyrus Townsend Brady’s quote. Made by Rowland & Marcellus Co., Staffordshire, England. 4. Vestry Organization and Cemetery Deed Vestry Meeting (April 25, 1911) : The newly elected vestry organized, electing Charles Wells Walker (warden), Frank Quigg (treasurer), S. Col. Summerill (secretary, after Leslie Jefferis declined), and Clayland Stephens Walker (rector’s warden, appointed by Burk). Convention delegates were Dobson, Hughes, and Walker. Mrs. Leslie Jefferis was named treasurer of the building fund, and Quigg for the cemetery. Cemetery Deed : Burk, Quigg, Sarah Swift Zulich, and Mr. and Mrs. Leslie Jefferis and Charles Wells Walker presented a deed for a 20-acre cemetery tract, subject to a $2,500 mortgage. The vestry resolved to open the main driveway and sought bids. First Interment : On April 28, 1911, Rev. Jesse Y. Burk, S.T.D., was reinterred from Woodlands Cemetery to the Washington Memorial Cemetery, with his son, Rev. W. Herbert Burk, officiating. 5. Communion Silver and Choir Vestments Silver : On May 14, 1911, Elle T. Lundy of Bronxville, N.Y., presented a solid silver chalice and paten in memory of her mother, Mary S. Lundy. The chalice, with a hexagonal base, bears the Washington arms, Colonial Dames insignia, and an inscription. The gold-lined paten features a cross, chapel arms, and “Thanks be to God who giveth us the victory.” The dedication service included Evening Prayer, with choir members Jane and Margaret Todd presenting the silver to Lundy, followed by dedicatory prayers led by Burk and the choir under Mary M. Hibbs. Vestments : Sarah Swift Zulich funded new choir vestments, sewn by congregation members at Burk’s residence on April 20. Mrs. S. Col. Summerill and Hannah Paxson Kirkbride were appointed to manage chorister vestments. 6. Guild Activities and Tea Room Guild Meeting (May 3) : Held in the Parish House, the Guild planned a coal fund, appointing collectors led by Mrs. Charles Wells Walker to gather 10-cent monthly contributions. A rummage sale was set for May 13. The meeting adjourned to serve Church Club delegates. Tea Room Donation : Mrs. Charles Lukens of Conshohocken donated 18 individual blue teapots. Needs include serving trays, paper napkins, a bread knife, and an ice pick. 7. History of Valley Forge (by Henry Woodman) Excerpt from Norristown Herald, August 14, 1850 (Letter XII) : Context : In early 1778, the Valley Forge encampment faced severe shortages of food, blankets, clothes, and shoes, with soldiers’ feet bleeding in the snow. Smallpox threatened, and provisions were nearly exhausted, with some troops going days without meat. Hardships : Despite Congress’s neglect, soldiers endured patiently, though some, influenced by anonymous letters from demagogues, considered deserting. Washington’s leadership prevented a revolt by reasoning with troops and appealing to Congress. Efforts : Nearly 3,000 soldiers were unfit for duty due to clothing shortages, requiring constant fires. Officers and soldiers carried wood and provisions like beasts of burden, while hospitals overflowed with the sick and wounded. Significance : The account highlights the army’s resilience and Washington’s critical role in maintaining unity. 8. Valley Forge Orderly Book Excerpts (February 8, 1778) , courtesy of George Clifford Thomas: Court-Martial (January 20–February 4) : William Moddock and Joseph Edwards, Pennsylvania residents, were convicted of attempting to drive cattle to the enemy, fined £100 each, and confined. Philip Kirk, John Williamson, David Dunn, and Daniel Williamson were convicted of supplying the enemy, with Kirk imprisoned and others sentenced to 200–250 lashes. James Brown and Jacob Gibson were acquitted. The Commander-in-Chief approved corporal punishments but remitted property confiscation, citing martial law limits. Market Regulations : A market opened at Stone Chimney Piquet on Mondays and Thursdays, and near the Adjutant General’s office on Wednesdays and Saturdays, with fixed prices and handbills distributed to enforce regulations. Significance : These entries reflect efforts to maintain discipline and regulate resources during the encampment. 9. Museum Donations Anna C. Pechin : Donated a pair of andirons from the Pechin homestead in Philadelphia, fine examples of early craftsmanship. Mrs. John W. Andrews : Gave a large hot cake griddle from the Zook homestead, possibly used when it served as headquarters for the Commissary General and General Morgan. 10. Community Events Housewarming (April 22) : Forty-three Sunday school workers, including Revs. James B. Halsey, Leigh Roy Urban, and Edward R. Noble, honored Burk with a housewarming, visiting the chapel in the rain for a brief service. Mrs. John Loman organized a supper served in Burk’s dining room. Transfer : Martha Spackman Grubb transferred to the Church of St. Luke and the Epiphany, Philadelphia, on May 3. 11. Administrative and Calendar Notes Leadership : Rev. W. Herbert Burk (rector), Frank Quigg (warden/treasurer), Charles Wells Walker (rector’s warden), S. Col. Summerill (secretary), Mary M. Hibbs (chorister), Mary Supplee Stephens (organist), William Rumford (sexton). Vestrymen listed above. Schedule : Includes services for Rogation Days (May 22–24), Ascension Day (May 25), Memorial Day (May 30, with burial office), Whitsunday (June 4), Ember Days (June 7, 9, 10), and Trinity Sunday (June 11). Guild meeting set for June 7. Services : Sunday services at 10:45 a.m. and 3:45 p.m., Sunday School at 2:30 p.m., Holy Communion on the first Sunday, and services at Stewart Fund Hall, King-of-Prussia. Grok AI contributed to this summary.

title: Washington Chapel Chronicle 4, no. 8 (November 1911): 57-64
author: W. Herbert Burk Washington Chapel Guild Emma W. Crawford
description: The November 15, 1911, issue of the Washington Chapel Chronicle (Vol. IV, No. 8), published by the Washington Chapel Guild at the Washington Memorial Chapel in Valley Forge, Pennsylvania, highlights the contributions of Revolutionary War patriots at Valley Forge, the success of the Harvest Home Festival, and new additions to the Valley Forge Museum. It also includes historical accounts of foreign officers and military discipline, alongside parish updates and upcoming events. Below is a summary of the key content: 1. Men of Valley Forge (Warren and Prescott Chapter, D.A.R., Boston) Patriots’ Profiles : The issue lists six Revolutionary soldiers who served at Valley Forge, with descendants in the Warren and Prescott Chapter, D.A.R.: Timothy Bigelow (1739–1790): Worcester blacksmith, led a disciplined Minute Men regiment, served at Saratoga, Valley Forge, Monmouth, and Quebec (captured, exchanged). Died in debtor’s prison; monument in Worcester. Descendant: Louise Bigelow. Parke Avery (1741–1821): Fought at Boston, New York, White Plains, Long Island, Valley Forge, and Fort Griswold (severely wounded). Re-enlisted in 1813–1814. Descendant: Mary H. Dobson. Samuel Greene Page (1753–1814): Captain in Tappan’s regiment, fought at Lexington, Monmouth, Stony Point, Valley Forge, and Delaware crossing. Descendant: Frances B. Greene (deceased). Jedediah Huntington (1743–1824): Harvard graduate, “Son of Liberty,” brigadier general, served at Dorchester Heights, New York, Valley Forge, and investigated Forts Montgomery and Clinton losses. Breveted major-general, later Collector of Customs. Descendant: Sarah H. Hooker. John Spering (1755–1846): Fought at Brandywine, Germantown, Monmouth, Valley Forge, and Delaware crossing. Lived to 91, followed Mexican War news. Descendant: Elisha M. Rees (deceased), Charles E. Jenkins (deceased). John White (1756–?): Served in Glover’s and Hutchinson’s regiments at Boston, Valley Forge, and Delaware crossing. Discharged after illness, later a prisoner in 1812. Descendants: Harriet Rose White, Emma S. White (resigned). 2. Harvest Home Festival Event Success : Held November 11, organized by S. Col. Summerill, it raised $117 for the Building Fund (net after expenses pending). The parish house was decorated with corn stalks, featuring autumn produce, livestock (pig, chickens, cat), preserves, and an oyster supper, reflecting congregational vitality and community spirit. 3. Valley Forge Museum Collections Montgomery County Generals : Mrs. William E. Montague donated a crayon portrait of General Winfield Scott Hancock. The museum lacks portraits of Generals Hartranft (except a cabinet photo), Slemmer, and Zook, urging local contributions to honor their national contributions. Hancock Artifacts : Dr. Alfred H. Read and Nina Boreiche Read donated an army order for Surgeon Louis B. Read to treat Hancock post-Gettysburg. The Mary Elizabeth Schofield Collection includes a card from President Andrew Johnson requesting Hancock’s visit, plus three Hancock letters. Hannah P. Kirkbride donated a Hartranft cabinet photo. S.J. Silcock Donation : Formerly Mrs. Cornelius P. Bergen, she gifted Lieutenant Bergen’s 1861–1862 diary (61st Regiment, Company E, N.Y.S.V.), newspapers on Lincoln’s funeral (1863), Garfield’s assassination (1881), and the Spanish-American War (1899). Martha Washington Bullard : Donated a 1770 Boston Gazette , an “Old Ironsides” account, and her father’s lines about Washington’s kindness to his grandmother on Powder Horn Hill. Museum Attendance : 261 admissions in October, indicating public interest. 4. Chapel and Community Updates Primary Department Contribution : Mrs. S. Col. Summerill and the primary class raised $15.64 (of $21.96) for a circulating boiler, installed for the Harvest Home Festival, solving hot water issues for large events. George Todd presented the funds. Missions Apportionment : The Men’s Auxiliary to the Board of Missions reported last year’s $85.25 contribution (exceeding the $50 goal) and set a $100 goal for 1911–1912, plus $25 for diocesan church extension. Duplex envelopes were encouraged for systematic giving. Thanksgiving Offering : Designated for Episcopal Hospital, Philadelphia, with fruit and vegetable gifts for Charity Hospital, Norristown. 5. Historical Accounts Valley Forge History by Henry Woodman (Norristown Herald, August 21, 1850) : Details foreign officers with Baron DeKalb, including Lafayette (quartered at Samuel Havard’s after Brandywine), Pulaski (at John Beaver’s widow’s house, died at Savannah), Kosciusko (later Polish commander, fell at Prague), Duhamel, Duponceau, Steuben, and Dubryson (lived in a cave near DeKalb’s quarters). Steuben’s cook, expecting luxury, quit after encountering primitive cooking conditions (“Steuben’s Kitchen”). Valley Forge Orderly Book (February 19–21, 1778) , courtesy of George Clifford Thomas: Orders searches for illegal liquor sales near camp, restricts provost guard to capital crimes, and announces a book auction. Capt. Madeira recovered baggage, and a board of officers deemed Major Ryon’s promotion irregular and settled Capt. Grier’s rank dispute. Virginia Line returns were ordered, and Ensign Porter found a large sum of money. 6. Parish Register and Calendar Baptisms : Hartranft Stockham (October 28). Marriages : Temple J. English and Mary Catharine Anderson (October 18); Stout Sherman and Annie Jardine Gordan (October 25); Joseph Reeves Merritt and Mary Estelle Low (November 5, Christ Church, Woodbury, N.J.). Calendar : Includes Trinity Sundays (November 19–26), Norristown Convocation (November 21), Thanksgiving (November 28), St. Andrew’s Day (November 30), Advent Sundays (December 3–10), Massachusetts Marker dedication and Washington Pew Screen unveiling (November 18), Guild meeting (December 6). Bishops’ Consecration : On October 28, Philip M. Rhinelander and Thomas J. Garland were consecrated Bishop Coadjutor and Bishop Suffragan of Pennsylvania, respectively, in a historic service at George W. South Memorial Church, Philadelphia. 7. Additional Notes Men and Religion Forward Movement : Chapel representatives include Clayland S. Walker (Boys’ Work), Frank Quigg (Social Service), Charles Wells Walker (Missions), Nathan M. Hughes (Evangelism), and Leslie Jefferis (Bible Study). Vestry Leadership : Rev. W. Herbert Burk (rector), Charles Wells Walker (vestry’s warden), Clayland Stephens Walker (rector’s warden), Frank Quigg (treasurer/cemetery treasurer), S. Col. Summerill (secretary), Leslie Jefferis (building fund treasurer), vestrymen (Edward H. Binns, Thomas H. Dobson, B. F. Fisher, Nathan B. Hughes), Mary M. Hibbs (chorister). Grok AI contributed to this summary.

title: 婦人衞生雜誌 1911.01 no. 254
author: 大日本婦人衛生会
description: The Fujin Eisei Zasshi (婦人衞生雜誌 "Women's Hygiene Journal") was a Japanese periodical published by the Greater Japan Women's Hygiene Association (大日本婦人衛生会). It was launched in 1888 as the organization's official organ (initially named 婦人衛生会雑誌 until 1893) and lasted until 1926. It was dedicated to the study of women's health and hygiene and is an important historical source in exploring the relationship between modern medicine and the focus on women's bodies as an object of research and a concern of public health. It was also a central publication in the broader rise of the modern concept of hygiene (衛生) and was aimed primarily at educated women readers. Ogino Ginko (荻野吟子 1851-1913), Japan's first female licensed physician, was a key leader in the association and also one of the founding editors of the journal with Matsuura Satoko (松浦里子 1861-1891).

title: 教育雜誌 1911.06 第三卷第六期
author: 商務印書館
description: 教育雜誌 (The Chinese Educational Review) was a monthly published in Shanghai by the Commercial Press from the beginning of 1909, founded under the editorship of Lufei Kui (陸費逵), and it is the longest-running and most influential education journal of modern China, appearing through the end of the Qing, the whole Republican period and the war years until 1948. Its standing sections — 言論 and 主張 for argument, 調查 for surveys, 實驗 for classroom experiment, 世界教育新潮 for foreign developments, 小學教育論壇, 記事 and 教育界消息 for news, 新刊介紹 for reviews, with 文藝 and plates — together amount to a continuous record of Chinese educational thought and practice across four decades. Nearly every question that mattered passed through it: the abolition of the examination system and the building of a modern school system, vernacular and simplified characters, vocational and mass education, coeducation and the schooling of girls, the reception of Dewey and of testing and measurement, and the improvisations forced on schools by the war. Because the Commercial Press was also the country's largest textbook publisher, the journal doubles as a window on how Chinese schooling was actually equipped. title: Concerning the spiritual in art
author: Wassily Kandinsky
description: A pioneering work in the movement to free art from its traditional bonds to material reality, this book is one of the most important documents in the history of modern art. Written by the famous nonobjective painter Wassily Kandinsky (1866-1944), it explains Kandinsky's own theory of painting and crystallizes the ideas that were influencing many other modern artists of the period. Along with his own ground-breaking paintings, this book had a tremendous impact on the development of modern art. The first part issues a call for a spiritual revolution in painting that will let artists express their own inner lives in abstract, non-material terms. Just as musicians do not depend upon the material world for their music, so artists should not have to depend upon the material world for their art.

This copy has been selected because of its suitability as a permanent reference copy. title: ERIC ED543042: Teaching Language through Agriculture and Domestic Science. Bulletin, 1912, No. 18. Whole Number 490
author: ERIC
description: One of the most difficult problems of modern school practice is how to prevent overcrowding the curriculum, breaking up the school day into small fragments of time devoted to disconnected tasks, and dissipating the energies of the children to such an extent that the process of education is hindered rather than helped by the attempts to enrich and modernize the courses of study. The solution of the problem lies in a closer correlation of subjects and especially of formal subjects with content subjects, and it is fortunate that when the correlation is well made both subjects can be better taught and in less time than either alone. This is especially true of language, the most effective learning of which comes, in the elementary grades, as a by-product of the right study of content subjects. How to teach language through the study of agriculture and domestic science is the theme of the accompanying manuscript by Prof. M. A. Leiper, of the Western Kentucky State Normal School. This bulletin is intended as a practical aid to rural teachers along a definite line which is clearly described in the text. [Best copy available has been provided.]

title: 婦人衞生雜誌 1912.04 no. 269
author: 大日本婦人衛生会
description: The Fujin Eisei Zasshi (婦人衞生雜誌 "Women's Hygiene Journal") was a Japanese periodical published by the Greater Japan Women's Hygiene Association (大日本婦人衛生会). It was launched in 1888 as the organization's official organ (initially named 婦人衛生会雑誌 until 1893) and lasted until 1926. It was dedicated to the study of women's health and hygiene and is an important historical source in exploring the relationship between modern medicine and the focus on women's bodies as an object of research and a concern of public health. It was also a central publication in the broader rise of the modern concept of hygiene (衛生) and was aimed primarily at educated women readers. Ogino Ginko (荻野吟子 1851-1913), Japan's first female licensed physician, was a key leader in the association and also one of the founding editors of the journal with Matsuura Satoko (松浦里子 1861-1891).
